scores.evidence: metrics.json has no hard failures: overflowX is false in all three shots, with no offenders, and consoleErrors, mermaidErrors, unknownBlocks and brokenImages are all 0. The one figure, s1-b2, is a 4-node flowchart TD. It reads clearly at 390 px with JP labels ユーザー / フロントエンド ブラウザの画面 / バックエンド サーバー / データベース and edge labels 操作する, 依頼と返事, 保存と取り出し (pages/mobile-jp-04.png). Its caption 図1 states the takeaway, and there is a 図の説明を読む disclosure (pages/mobile-jp-05.png, pages/desktop-jp-03.png). The JSON code block s2-b4 wraps inside its card on mobile without sideways scroll (pages/mobile-jp-07.png, pages/mobile-jp-08.png). There are no decorative images, and no screen shows personal data.

textOnlyScreens is empty for all three shots. The desktop JP median is 40 chars per line, at the top of the 30-40 target (max 55). The desktop EN median is 74 (target 60-75, max 81). Every screen has a heading, callout, definitions table, figure, prompt card, steps or quiz. The longest runs are the 6-step worked example ex-steps (pages/mobile-jp-16.png to pages/mobile-jp-19.png) and the 4-question check-quiz (pages/mobile-jp-24.png to pages/mobile-jp-27.png). Each step has its own expected-result box and each question its own card, so neither reads as a wall of text.

The EN screenshots have no leftover Japanese. This covers the diagram (User / Frontend screen in the browser / Backend server / Database, pages/desktop-en-03.png), the prompt-card placeholders 'how to show finished tasks', 'field to add', 'current state' and 'change you want' (pages/desktop-en-06.png, pages/desktop-en-10.png), the quiz options, the checklist, the flashcards and the wrap-up (pages/desktop-en-15.png to pages/desktop-en-20.png). Text contrast is good. The answer buttons, step checkboxes and the 続ける/Continue card all sit clear of the 56 px top bar and the 60 px bottom bar on mobile (pages/mobile-jp-10.png, pages/mobile-jp-30.png).

niceToHave: Step titles in ex-steps and practice-steps start with their own number (「① 足りないものを書き出す」, '1. List what is missing'), and the reader already draws a numbered circle next to each step. So every step shows its number twice (pages/mobile-jp-16.png, pages/desktop-jp-11.png, pages/desktop-en-11.png). You could drop the ①–⑥ / '1.'–'6.' prefixes from the step titles. Then check that the practice-steps hint 「1-5の手順⑤」 / 'step 5 of 1-5' still matches the reader's circle numbers.

On mobile JP, a few short quiz options wrap so that one kana or a word fragment sits alone on the second line. Examples: 「しまってお／く」 (s1-check option c, pages/mobile-jp-05.png), 「変える／る」 (s2-check option a, pages/mobile-jp-10.png) and 「いな／いから」 (hook-predict option a, pages/mobile-jp-02.png). A slightly shorter or longer wording would avoid this, for example 「支出の記録を整理してしまっておく」 without the comma.
On desktop JP, the checklist item pc-input breaks so that 「す」 sits alone on the second line (「…書いてありま／す」, pages/desktop-jp-14.png). You could shorten it, for example 「画面側の依頼で、読み終えた日を入力してAPIで保存しています」.
On mobile JP, summary-points point 1 splits 「フロントエン／ド」 across lines (pages/mobile-jp-27.png).

reader: in ex-steps step ex-split on mobile, a line starts with 「、保存と一覧の…」 right after the dotted glossary link データベース. The inline term link seems to break the line-start rule (kinsoku) for the comma that follows it (pages/mobile-jp-17.png).

summary: metrics.json records lessonHash sha256:1d967dfe70f0b1a4, the same hash I was given. It shows no hard failures: no overflow, and no console, Mermaid, unknown-block or broken-image errors. Every screen has a structural element. I opened all 30 mobile-jp, 20 desktop-jp and 20 desktop-en screens and found no personal data on any of them. The main strength is the top-to-bottom 4-node architecture diagram with JP and EN labels, which reads well at 390 px, together with fully localized prompt cards and quizzes. There is nothing that must be fixed. The most useful polish is to drop the duplicated step numbers (①/'1.') from the step titles and to reword a few quiz options that leave a single kana on a line on mobile.
